results.problem: 3-DSR-ML (3-Dimensional Stable Roommates with Master List of 2-sets)
MDSR-Poset (Multidimensional Stable Roommates with master poset of agents)
results.bound: O(n) time (or O(n^2) time if the poset is given via pairwise comparisons)
results.quote: Proposition 4.1. If \\unknown_\\mathrm{ML} is a strict order, then any MDSR-Poset instance admits a uniquely determined stable matching. Assuming that the poset is given as a ranking a_1\\succ_\\mathrm{ML}a_2\\succ_\\mathrm{ML}\\cdots\\succ_\\mathrm{ML}a_n, this stable matching can be found in O(n) time, where n is the number of agents. If the poset is given via pairwise comparisons, then the unique stable matching can be found in O(n^2) time.

Proposition 4.4. MDSR-Poset can be solved in O(n^2)+(\\kappa d^4)^{O(\\kappa d^4)}n time, where \\kappa is the maximum number of agents incomparable to a single agent, d is the dimension (i.e., the group size), and n is the number of agents.

Theorem 4.6. MDSR-Poset can be solved in O(n^2)+(\\kappa^52^{16\\kappa})^{O(\\kappa^52^{16\\kappa})}n time, where \\kappa is the maximum number of agents an agent is incomparable to, and n is the total number of agents.
Theorem 4.15. 3DSR-Poset parameterized by poset width is W[1]-hard.

results.bound: W[1]-hard parameterized by \\lambda(\\mathcal{I}) (deletion distance to a strictly ordered master poset)
results.quote: Theorem 4.27. 3-DSR parameterized by \\lambda(\\mathcal{I}) is W[1]-hard, where \\lambda(\\mathcal{I}) denotes the minimum number of agents such that the preferences of the instance arising through the deletion of these agents are derived from a strict order.

results.problem: 3-DSRI-ML (3-Dimensional Stable Roommates with Incomplete preferences and Master List)
results.bound: NP-complete, even if the master poset is a strict order
results.quote: Theorem 4.34. 3-DSRI-ML is NP-complete, even if the master poset is a strict order.
